cover: Khartoum denies strike; UN probe sought

stories.label: World · Life & safety
stories.head: Deaths despite the ceasefire
bullets: Strikes and gunfire killed at least four people in Gaza City, Khan Younis, near Nuseirat and near Jabalia.
A woman was shot near Jabalia.
Israel's military says it struck Hamas in three places and was not aware of the Jabalia incident.

stories.label: World · Life & safety
stories.head: Who struck the market?
bullets: Sudan's foreign ministry says the army has 'absolutely no connection' to Monday's strike; it gave no evidence.
RSF-aligned authorities, who blame the army, asked the UN fact-finding mission to investigate.
Officials say the dead were buried in two mass graves; the African Union condemned the strikes.

stories.label: India · Assembly · Land
stories.head: Sit-in against the Siang dam
bullets: A 24-hour sit-in began on Thursday against the 11,000 MW Siang Upper project.
Protesters want detained activists freed and surveys stopped; five more were reportedly taken into custody.
The district allowed the sit-in but barred marches, and says law and order is separate from dam opposition.

stories.label: India · Assembly
stories.head: Sit-ins over the Sunurok killings
bullets: Sit-ins were held across the valley districts and schools stayed shut.
Security forces clashed with student marchers near Kangla Gate; several people were detained.
No police or government statement on Thursday's protests was reported.
